subject.title: fix(plugins): prevent npm 12 metadata failures from disabling healthy plugins

question: Which branch should become the canonical fix for https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/106189, and should the npm 12 update-check parser change land with the state-preservation fix?
rationale: Both open PRs address the destructive plugin-state transition, but only https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107063 has real CLI proof and only this PR includes the sibling update-check parser normalization; automation cannot safely choose which evidence or scope to discard.

options.title: Adopt the proven branch and port parser fix
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107063 as the canonical state-preservation patch, then add this PR's focused update-check singleton-array normalization if current main still needs it.

options.title: Retain this broader branch
options.body: Rebase this PR and require a redacted real openclaw update repair or plugins update state-transition transcript before treating it as the canonical landing branch.

options.title: Land state fix only
options.body: Choose the narrower state-preservation patch and track the update-check parser compatibility separately only if maintainers confirm that surface remains user-reachable and broken.

recommendation.title: Adopt the proven branch and port parser fix
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107063 as the canonical state-preservation patch, then add this PR's focused update-check singleton-array normalization if current main still needs it.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the update-check parser and disable-on-failure policy attributed to his earlier work.
